variants.answer: I’d model the transaction lifecycle as a discriminated union so each state has the data it actually needs—for example, `pending` may include a start time, `success` a transaction ID, and `failure` an error message. In the UI, I’d switch exhaustively on `status` to show a loading indicator, confirmation, or actionable error, with a `never` check so TypeScript catches unhandled states. I’d also disable duplicate submissions while pending and test each transition. In a fictional project, this approach reduced invalid state combinations and made it easier to add a retry flow later.
